chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Qāsim ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAlī ibn Abī Ḥamzah, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
"The hand of the thief is not cut off until his theft reaches a quarter of a dinar; and ʿAlī عليه السلام cut off [the hand] for a helmet of iron."

ʿAlī said: And Abū Baṣīr said: I asked Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام about the minimum amount for which the thief's hand is cut off, so he said: "For an iron helmet." I said: "And what is its price?" He said: "A quarter of a dinar."

key_terms.السَّارِقِ: the thief subject to the legal ruling of theft
key_terms.بَيْضَةِ حَدِيدٍ: an iron helmet, cited as an example of property at that value
key_terms.تُقْطَعُ: is cut off, referring to the prescribed legal punishment
key_terms.رُبُعَ دِينَارٍ: a quarter of a dinar, the minimum legal threshold mentioned here
key_terms.سَرِقَتُهُ: the amount or item he stole

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum amount for which a thief's hand is cut off in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal threshold at which the hand of a thief is cut off: the stolen property must reach the value of a quarter of a dinar. It also cites the practice of Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام and clarifies that an iron helmet was regarded as having that value.
